extracted.intended_audience: students of advanced calculus / mathematical analysis (undergraduate/first-year graduate), French-speaking
extracted.subtask_description: Methods, formulas and procedural rules for computing double and triple integrals, surface areas, Beta/Gamma (Euler) integrals, and applying Green/Gauss theorems. Includes worked examples (polar coordinates, spherical surface, volume comparisons) and remarks about limits and special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume as a double integral over base
rubrics_metrics.description: Le volume V d'un solide dont la hauteur (ou fonction) z=f(x,y) est déterminée au-dessus d'une aire plane C est donné par V = ∬_C f(x,y) dσ (le texte: "Le volume V est alors ... l'intégrale étant étendue à l'aire du demi-cercle de base.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute V by summing infinitesimal 'tranches' or elements: for each element of base area dσ multiply par la valeur de la hauteur f(x,y), puis intégrer sur C. Use whichever coordinate system (rectangular or polar) makes the limits/simple form convenient; examples given with semi-circle base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of polar coordinates for plane area elements
rubrics_metrics.description: En coordonnées polaires dans le plan des xy, l'élément d'aire s'écrit dσ = r dr dθ (le texte: "dio = r dθ dr").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converting a double integral to polar coordinates, substitute x = r cosθ, y = r sinθ and take dσ = r dr dθ. Choose r and θ limits according to the projection region. Examples: semi-circle base with r from 0 to a cosθ, θ from 0 to π/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration by radial slices (fix θ, integrate r)
rubrics_metrics.description: Méthode consistant à faire la somme des éléments compris entre deux rayons OP et OP' faisant un angle dθ — pour ces éléments θ et dθ sont constants et r varie entre r_1(θ) et r_2(θ) (ex.: "La tranche T ... r varie de 0 à OM_1 = a cosθ").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the contribution T(θ) = ∫_{r1(θ)}^{r2(θ)} f(r,θ) r dr for each θ, then integrate T(θ) over θ. Handle cases where r_1 may be 0. Example: evaluate first the inner r–integral to obtain T(θ) then integrate over θ from θ_min to θ_max.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration by annular crowns (fix r, integrate θ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Autre façon: commencer par sommer les éléments situés entre deux cercles de centre O et rayons r et r+dr; pour un r fixé on intègre θ entre θ_1(r) et θ_2(r) (le texte: "on peut commencer par faire la somme des éléments ... compris entre deux cercles ... ces deux cercles découpent ... une tranche ayant la forme d'une couronne").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each r compute T(r) = ∫_{θ1(r)}^{θ2(r)} f(r,θ) dθ (multiplying by r dr if using dσ = r dr dθ), then integrate T(r) over r from r_min to r_max. This is convenient when angle-limits are simple functions of r; the text gives the explicit conversion and when to prefer this order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle multiple intersections of a ray with boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: Remarque: si un rayon vecteur issu de O coupait la courbe C en plus de deux points, il la couperait en un nombre pair de points (le texte: "il entrerait dans C en M_1, sortirait en M_2, rentrerait en M_3, ressortirait en M_4 ... il faudrait alors intégrer par rapport à r de r_1 à r_2, puis de r_3 à r_4, ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a ray intersects the domain boundary in more than two points, decompose the radial integration into the union of radial intervals inside the region and sum the corresponding integrals. Always account for an even number of crossings and sum over each entering-exiting pair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust limits when the pole/origin lies inside the base region
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications à apporter quand l'origine est dans le champ d'intégration — il faut modifier les valeurs des limites des deux intégrations et sommer des cylindres/couronnes en conséquence (le texte: "quand O est dans la base, il faut modifier évidemment les valeurs des limites des deux intégrations").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the origin is inside the projection region, split the integration domain into parts so that for each chosen integration order the variable limits are well-defined (e.g., for small r you'll get complete crowns with θ from 0 to 2π, for larger r you get partial angles). The text details summing piles from r=0 to r_interior and then from r_interior to r_exterior with appropriate θ-limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface area by projection: dS via angle with base plane
rubrics_metrics.description: Projection method: the area of a small facet A_a projects to A_co on the xy-plane and A_a = A_co / cos α where α is angle between facet plane and xy-plane (le texte: "Aa = Ac_o / cos a ... a désignant l'angle aigu du plan de la face ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get surface area S of z = f(x,y), project the surface onto the xy-plane and correct by the secant of the angle between tangent plane and xy-plane. Passing to the limit yields the integrand factor related to partial derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for surface area of a graph z = f(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pour z = f(x,y) avec p = ∂z/∂x et q = ∂z/∂y, le facteur est sqrt(1 + p^2 + q^2) so that S = ∬_C sqrt(1 + p^2 + q^2) dx dy (le texte: "F(x,y) étant une fonction connue ... S = ∬ F(x,y) dσ" and earlier derivation giving F = √(1+p^2+q^2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute partial derivatives p and q; integrand is √(1+p^2+q^2). Evaluate the double integral over the projection region C using rectangular or polar coordinates as convenient. The textbook derives this from the limit of planar facets tending to the tangent plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute spherical surface portions by projection
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: for a sphere x^2+y^2+z^2 = a^2, the cosine of the angle between tangent plane and xy-plane is z/a and the surface area of a portion projects to ∬ z dσ appropriately (text: "Il est d'ailleurs évident géométriquement que cos A = -z/a ... écrivant que la projection de OM sur Oz est ... z = a cos γ").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the special simplifications for sphere: express z in polar coordinates (z = sqrt(a^2 - r^2) or z = a cos φ) and evaluate the surface area integral using dσ = r dr dθ combined with the appropriate factor derived from geometry. The text works a semi-circle example in polar coordinates to compute a spherical cap area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viviani's theorem (spherical partition example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Théorème de Viviani — in the configuration of figure 184 the curve K dividing the eighth of sphere produces an exterior part whose area equals the square of side a (texto: "Cette partie extérieure est donc équivalente au carré de côté a. C'est là le théorème de Viviani.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use partitioning of spherical octant and area calculations via projection to relate the area S of a portion to the remaining part and deduce special equalities (the textbook presents this as an application/example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Euler integral of the first kind (Beta function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Définition: l'intégrale eulérienne de première espèce B(a,b) = ∫_0^1 t^{a-1} (1-t)^{b-1} dt, valable pour a>0, b>0 (le texte: "on appelle intégrale eulérienne de première espèce l'intégrale ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties include symmetry B(a,b)=B(b,a) (proved by change of variable). Use substitutions (e.g., t = sin^2 φ) to transform integrals to trigonometric forms when helpful. The text gives examples of variable changes to evaluate or relate Beta integrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and recurrence of Euler integral of the second kind (Gamma function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Définition: T(a) = Γ(a) = ∫_0^∞ t^{a-1} e^{-t} dt for a>0. Recurrence: Γ(a) = (a-1) Γ(a-1), and for integer a, Γ(n) = (n-1)! (le texte: "T(a) = (a-1) T(a-1) ... si a est un entier positif, T(a) = 1·2·...·(a-1)").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integration by parts to obtain the recurrence. Repeated application reduces evaluation to a parameter in (1,2] where numerical tables or other formulas can be used. Note Γ(1)=1 and Γ(0) diverges to infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction formula: Beta expressed via Gamma
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction by computing the same volume in Cartesian and polar coordinates leads to the identity relating Beta and Gamma functions (text develops equality of two expressions of a volume to obtain the desired formula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up an appropriate integral (e.g., evaluate a particular volume using rectangular coordinates then polar coordinates), identify expressions involving Γ and B, and equate them to derive relations like B(a,b) = Γ(a) Γ(b) / Γ(a+b). The textbook demonstrates this via the surface r = a x^{...} e^{-...} and volume computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of numerical tables and reduction for Gamma/Beta evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables give values (example: table of log Γ(1/2) for a between 0 and 1) and one uses the recurrence Γ(a) = (a-1)Γ(a-1) to reduce any argument to 1≤a≤2 to read off from tables (le texte: "on trouvera ... une table donnant les valeurs de log r(1/2) ... permet de calculer la valeur de r(a) ... ramener l'argument ... entre 1 et 2").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating Γ or B numerically, use recurrence relations to shift parameter into tabulated range; then use the table values or relations to compute the desired value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and decomposition approach for triple integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Définition: integrale triple ∭_V f(x,y,z) dV obtained by subdividing volume V into infinitesimal elements dV (text: "L'expression de dV est différente selon le système de coordonnées ... en coordonnées rectangulaires dv = dx dy dz").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute triple integrals by iterated integration: choose an order (e.g., integrate in z first between z_lower(x,y) and z_upper(x,y) for each base point (x,y), then integrate over projection region C). The textbook describes decomposing the domain into piles/parallelepipeds and summing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to compute triple integral by stacks (integrate z first)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method: pick an element dx dy in the projection C; form the prism above it whose z-limits are z_1(x,y) and z_2(x,y); for that prism P = dx dy ∫_{z1}^{z2} f(x,y,z) dz, then integrate P over C (le texte: "La somme des éléments ... correspondante à cette pile ... P = dx dy ∫_{z1}^{z2} f(x,y,z) dz").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces the triple integral to a double integral: I = ∬_C [∫_{z1(x,y)}^{z2(x,y)} f(x,y,z) dz] dx dy. The text emphasizes that the limits z1,z2 are functions of x and y determined by the bounding surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility of integration order for triple integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Remarque: on peut d'abord intégrer par rapport à z en rangeant les parallélépipèdes par piles parallèles à Oz; on pourrait de même intégrer d'abord par rapport à x ou y (le texte: "On pourrait, de même, intégrer d'abord par rapport à x ou y ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the integration order that yields simpler limits or integrands; reorganize the elemental decomposition accordingly (piles parallel to chosen axis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Green/Gauss divergence theorem (relation between volume integral and surface integral)
rubrics_metrics.description: Théorème (formule de Green): For a volume V bounded by closed surface S and continuous functions F,G,H with suitable derivatives, ∭_V (∂F/∂x + ∂G/∂y + ∂H/∂z) dV = ∬_S (F a + G b + H c) dS where a,b,c are direction cosines of outward normal (text: full derivation and statement, e.g. "Nous démontrerons ... la formule suivante" and subsequent equations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coordinate decomposition (prism over dx dy) and the fundamental theorem for one-variable integrals to transform the triple integral of divergence into surface integrals of normal components. The text gives special cases (e.g., expressing volume by surface integral) and prescribes continuity and boundedness conditions on functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of normal derivative
rubrics_metrics.description: The derivative of a function along the outward normal at a surface point is defined as the limit Δf/Δn when moving along the normal vector; in coordinates it equals a ∂f/∂x + b ∂f/∂y + c ∂f/∂z where a,b,c are direction cosines (text: "On désigne cette limite par ..." and derivation showing the Taylor expansion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this notion when expressing flux or boundary-normal derivatives in surface integrals; derive by Taylor expansion along the normal vector and pass to the limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when parallels to axes meet surface in more than two points
rubrics_metrics.description: Remarque: si les parallèles aux axes rencontraient la surface en plus de deux points, elles la rencontreraient en un nombre pair de points; le même raisonnement montre que les formules (Green, triple integrals) restent générales (texte: "Si ces parallèles la rencontraient en plus de deux points ... la formule de Green est générale").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When axis-parallels intersect the surface multiple times, decompose the domain into appropriate subdomains and sum contributions; the general integral formulas remain valid after accounting for alternating entering/exiting intersections.
